timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: ListAgents
tools.description: Lists agents you can SendMessage to — in-process subagents you spawned, the teammates on your team, other local Claude sessions on this machine, your Claude sessions running in the cloud (when this session has cloud access; a cloud session receives your message but cannot message any session back yet — do not ask it to reply, read its answer in its own transcript), and (when Remote Control is connected here) your account's other sessions — Remote Control sessions on other machines and cloud sessions, each row labeled by kind. Names are the address: send with `SendMessage({to: "<name>", message: "..."})`, copying the name exactly as a row prints it. Append a row's ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — two rows share it, or an error asks you to disambiguate.

channel.description: Not available in this build; leave unset.

q.description: Not available in this build; leave unset.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: SendMessage
tools.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

tools.name: ShareOnboardingGuide
tools.description:
Upload the ONBOARDING.md in the current directory and return a share link teammates can open in Claude Code. Call this after the user has confirmed the final content.

When called with the default mode='check': if a local ONBOARDING.md is present, uploads it to the most-recently-updated org guide (or creates one if none exist) and returns a fresh link. If no local file is present, returns the existing link without uploading (status: has_existing).

mode.description: 'check' (default): if ONBOARDING.md is present locally, uploads it to the most-recent guide (creates one if none exist); otherwise reports the existing link without uploading. 'update': upload to a specific guide by short_code. 'create': always make a new link. 'delete': remove the guide named by short_code; with no short_code, nothing is deleted and the user's guides are listed.

short_code.description: Short code of one guide, from an earlier call's result. Required by delete. With check or update, targets that guide instead of the most recently updated one.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: DeferredToolPlaceholder
tools.description: Reserved placeholder that keeps deferred tool loading active; never call this tool.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

content.text: Tool loaded.

lastPrompt: go ahead and use sub or parallel agents for all the tickets

input.message:
Main now has ticket 08 merged (commit 89c1e5d): inc02–inc10 scenarios and stricter guard tests in tests/test_answer_key_isolation.py. Your ticket 04 code must pass them when I merge, so please check them before you commit. Run `git merge main` in your worktree, or read the file with `git show main:tests/test_answer_key_isolation.py`.

The rules:
(1) No file under src/incident_investigator other than dataset.py may contain the literal incident IDs inc01–inc10. The only exception is the exact string "e.g. inc01" in cli.py. The same goes for any answer-key root-cause service name, such as checkout-svc. This applies to .py/.md/.json/.toml files, including mock.py and prompts.
(2) Only dataset.py may use DATA_DIR or build a path to the "data" folder.
(3) Other modules may import only load_scenario, list_incident_ids and UnknownIncidentError from dataset.
(4) A runtime test runs investigate(incident_id, MockLLM()) on all 10 incidents and must not touch answer keys. Your multi-agent MockLLM must therefore run cleanly end to end on every incident, including ones with scheduled tool timeouts, partials and errors. Merging main into your branch before your final test run is the easiest way to confirm this.

Ticket 08 is merged, so `main` now has 01, 02, 03 and 08. The full suite passes (143 tests) and pyright is clean.

**What 08 added:**
- **Dataset:** inc02 to inc10, each with 2 or 3 traps and its answer key in a separate folder. If you'd rather score these differently, tell me before 09 starts. The 08 ticket file has a one-line summary of every incident's root cause and traps for your realism review.

04 (planner and parallel DAG) and 12 (optional backends) are still running.

content.text:
Ticket 12 is merged, so `main` now has tickets 01, 02, 03, 08 and 12. All 206 tests pass and pyright is clean.

**What 12 added:**
- **Two new LLM backends:** `anthropic_api` (uses `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) and `openai_compat` (Ollama, LM Studio or vLLM).
- **Per-role choice:** `models.toml` now sets a backend and a model for each role. The defaults are unchanged: every role still uses the Claude CLI.
- **The `--llm` flag:** with no value, each role uses the backend from `models.toml`. With a value, that backend is used for every role.
- **New dependencies:** `anthropic` 2.8.0 and `httpx` 0.28.1.

**Live checks:** Ollama was already running on your machine, so the agent ran inc01 on a local `qwen2.5:7b` model. It found the right answer (a bad deploy on checkout-svc) in about 7 seconds. `anthropic_api` was not run live, because there is no API key.

**One loose end:** the graph still takes a single LLM client, so per-role backends only partly apply. I've asked the ticket 04 agent to pull in today's `main` and adopt per-role routing if it's cheap, or log it as still to do.

**Still open:** inc07 and inc10 each name a root-cause service that could be argued either way. Ticket 09 will score against those answers unless you say otherwise.

Ticket 04 (planner and parallel DAG) is still running. Tickets 05 and 06 start once it merges.

"""Post-processing between the investigation and the report (seam for ticket 05).

Ticket 05 replaces the body of `apply_evidence_rules` with the deterministic rules
(drop or demote Facts citing unknown IDs, cap unsupported hypotheses at 0.5, lower
confidence by 0.1 per open gap). It reads only the blackboard, so the single-agent
baseline (ticket 07) can call the same function.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from incident_investigator.blackboard import Blackboard
from incident_investigator.schemas import Hypothesis


def apply_evidence_rules(board: Blackboard) -> list[Hypothesis]:
    """Return the hypotheses with `final_confidence` set. Today: final = proposed."""
    return [h.model_copy(update={"final_confidence": h.proposed_confidence}) for h in board.hypotheses]


def rank(hypotheses: list[Hypothesis]) -> list[Hypothesis]:
    """Highest final confidence first; ties keep the Reasoning agent's order."""
    return sorted(hypotheses, key=lambda h: h.final_confidence or 0.0, reverse=True)

def rank(hypotheses: list[Hypothesis]) -> list[Hypothesis]:
    """Highest final confidence first; ties keep the Reasoning agent's order."""
    return sorted(hypotheses, key=lambda h: h.final_confidence or 0.0, reverse=True)

input.prompt:
Implement ticket 05 in this repo (a Python 3.12 uv project: LangGraph + Pydantic, multi-agent production incident investigator). You are in your own git worktree; commit your work there on the current branch. Do NOT push, add a remote, or touch the main checkout.

**Ticket:** `.scratch/incident-investigator/issues/05-evidence-rules-and-inconclusive.md` — read it fully, plus context: `incident-investigator-ai-ready-prd.md` (user-journey step 7, data model: Fact/Assumption/Hypothesis/EvidenceGap/InvestigationReport) and `DECISIONS.md` Q16, Q21 and the glossary. Read the `## Comments` of tickets 01–04 under `.scratch/incident-investigator/issues/` (04's comment describes the seam for you).

**Current code (01, 02, 03, 04, 08, 12 merged):** `evidence_rules.py` has the seam `apply_evidence_rules(board) -> list[Hypothesis]` (today final = proposed) and `rank()`. `blackboard.py` (Blackboard: incident_id, incident, tasks, findings, evidence = every row any tool returned, hypotheses, gaps (EvidenceGap has `tool, reason, affects_hypotheses, task_id`), failures, counters, trace, critic_loops, report), `graph.py` (planner → schedule/DAG waves → reasoning → `_after_evidence_rules` → reporting), `agents/` (planner, specialists, prompts, loop), `schemas.py`, `investigate.py` (returns `Investigation{report, blackboard}`). `uv sync` in your worktree first; then `uv run pytest` (full suite ~15 s) and `uv run pyright`.

**What to build (deterministic code, never the LLM):** (1) a Fact citing an evidence ID that does not exist is not kept as a Fact — move it to Assumptions (with a basis saying which cited IDs were invalid and how to verify) or drop it, and log every such change in a structured, inspectable way (e.g. a list of rule-adjustment records on the blackboard and/or report). Decide and document what "exists" means: IDs actually returned by tools during this run (`board.evidence`) is the recommended definition — the rules must not read the Scenario. Apply the same check to hypothesis supporting/contradicting IDs (drop unknown IDs, logged). (2) A Hypothesis with no supporting Fact is capped at 0.5 — define "supporting Fact" precisely (e.g. at least one kept Fact cites one of its supporting_ids) and document it. (3) Each open EvidenceGap that affects a Hypothesis lowers it by 0.1 — define "affects" (the gap's `affects_hypotheses` if set; otherwise decide a sensible deterministic rule, e.g. a gap affects hypotheses about the service/tool it blocked — document it), floor at 0. (4) If no hypothesis reaches 0.6 final confidence → outcome `INCONCLUSIVE`, and the report still lists the ranked hypotheses and the gaps. (5) The report lists Facts and Assumptions separately, and every recommended action is linked to an existing hypothesis id (drop or log actions pointing nowhere). Make this one shared post-processing function the single-agent baseline (ticket 07) can call with its own blackboard.

You own `evidence_rules.py`, the reporting step's use of it, and new report fields for rule adjustments if you add any. Keep edits to `graph.py` minimal (only the call site of the rules/report assembly); don't touch the Critic/limit areas. If you add fields to `InvestigationReport` in `schemas.py`, add them at the end with defaults to ease merging.

**Method:** test-first, red → green, one rule per slice. Agreed seam: `apply_evidence_rules` (or the shared post-processing function you create) on hand-built Blackboards — expected values as literal numbers from the spec (e.g. 0.8 proposed, no supporting fact → 0.5; two affecting gaps → 0.3) — plus one end-to-end test via `investigate()` with the mock LLM showing an INCONCLUSIVE outcome still lists hypotheses and gaps (e.g. inc09 or a mocked scenario). No tests of private helpers. Run pyright and single test files often; full `uv run pytest` at the end.

**Finish:** tick the ticket's truly-done checkboxes (explain any not), append a dated `## Comments` note (definitions you chose; how 07 calls the shared function), and commit with message `Ticket 05: <summary>` ending with `Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>`. content.text:
Ticket 04 is merged. `main` now has tickets 01, 02, 03, 04, 08 and 12, with 223 tests passing and pyright clean.

**What 04 added:**
- **Planner:** one planning call to the model turns the incident into a list of tasks with dependencies.
- **Task runner:** plain Python runs tasks with no dependency between them in parallel. Agents share a typed blackboard that holds the incident report but never the scenario, so they only learn about the incident by calling tools.
- **Repeatable failures:** tools are called in a fixed order across parallel tasks, so a scheduled tool failure always lands on the same task.
- **Per-role models:** the graph now gives each role its own backend, which finishes ticket 12's loose end.
- **Trace file:** the CLI now also saves the full blackboard as `<id>__multi.trace.json`.
- **Live run on inc01:** it found the right answer (bad deploy on checkout-svc, 0.8) ahead of three competing hypotheses. It took 77 s, with 15 LLM calls and 8 tool calls.

**Departures from the ticket:**
- Reporting is a fixed final step rather than a planned task. Code ranks the hypotheses, and the model only writes the recommended actions.
- The ticket asked for supporting and contradicting evidence on each hypothesis, but code only checks that there are at least two with supporting evidence. Contradicting evidence isn't required, so the model isn't pushed to invent it. In the live run the top hypothesis had none.

Tickets 05 (evidence rules and INCONCLUSIVE outcome) and 06 (Critic loop and run limits) are running now. Ticket 07 (single-agent baseline) starts once both are merged.

Ticket 05 is merged. `main` now has tickets 01–05, 08 and 12, with 241 tests passing and pyright clean.

**How the evidence rules work (all plain code, never the model):**
- **What counts as real evidence:** an evidence ID counts only if a tool actually returned it during this run.
- **Bad citations:** a Fact that cites an unknown ID becomes an Assumption that names the bad IDs. It is never dropped silently. Unknown IDs on a hypothesis, and actions that point to no hypothesis, are removed.
- **Confidence:** a hypothesis with no supporting Fact is capped at 0.5. Each evidence gap that affects it takes off 0.1. When a gap doesn't name the hypotheses it affects, a fixed table maps each tool to the root-cause categories it covers.
- **Outcome:** if no hypothesis reaches 0.6, the outcome is INCONCLUSIVE, and the report still lists the ranked hypotheses and the gaps.
- **Audit log:** every change the rules make is recorded on the report as a `rule_adjustment`.

**Limits to know about:**
- **inc09 with the mock:** the offline mock reaches ROOT_CAUSE at exactly 0.6 on inc09, which is meant to be inconclusive. So the end-to-end INCONCLUSIVE test uses a scripted run on inc01 instead. This affects only mock runs, but it is another reason mock runs say nothing about accuracy.
- **Gaps don't record the service:** a gap doesn't record which service the failed query was about, so it lowers hypotheses about any service.
- **Gaps never close:** every gap counts as open for the whole run.

I've told the 06 agent (Critic loop and run limits, still running) to pull in 05 and where the small conflict will be. Ticket 07 (single-agent baseline) starts once 06 merges.

content.text:
Ticket 06 is merged. `main` now has tickets 01–06, 08 and 12, with 255 tests passing and pyright clean.

**What 06 added:**
- **Critic loop:** a Critic agent reviews the hypotheses and can add follow-up tasks. These go back through the scheduler, for at most 2 extra loops.
- **Run limits:** the run stops at 30 tool calls, 300k tokens or 10 minutes. Each limit sets its own `terminated_by` value, and a report is still written from whatever the blackboard holds at that point.
- **Agent failures:** an agent that fails twice is recorded on the report's new `failures` field, and the run carries on without it.
- **Shared limits:** all the limit values live in one `limits.py`, so the baseline can use the same object.

**Departures from the ticket:**
- **Third Critic call:** the Critic is asked once more after loop 2, so the run can tell `critic_limit` (it still wanted more) apart from `done`.
- **Reporting after a hard stop:** when the token or time limit stops the run, the report has no recommended actions, because the model call that writes them is skipped.
- **Task stopped by a limit:** it is marked `failed`, but no AgentFailure is recorded.
- **Wall clock:** the 10-minute limit can't stop a model call that's already running. Each call is still capped at 120 s, so a run can go about 2 minutes over.

**Test speed:** the suite went from 15 s to 44 s. The cause is real retry delays in the tool layer during mock runs. I've asked the ticket 07 agent to make those delays injectable and set them to zero in tests, without weakening any test.

Ticket 07 (single-agent baseline) is running. Once it merges, 09 (evaluation) and 11 (HTTP API) run in parallel, then 10 (LLM judge), then 13 (docs). Before 09 starts, decide whether inc07 and inc10 keep their current root-cause service names in the answer keys. Without an answer, 09 will score against them as they are.

  - `mode` is `Literal["multi", "single"]`; `MODES` lists both. An unknown mode raises `ValueError`.
  - The CLI's `--mode single` writes `<id>__single.json` and `<id>__single.trace.json`, the same two files as multi mode.
  
  **Files changed:**
  - New: `src/incident_investigator/baseline.py` (`run_baseline`) and `tests/test_baseline.py` (15 tests).

  - **Tool budget:** the baseline is one task, so the per-task cap of 6 does not apply. The run's 30-call budget is the binding limit. `run_agent` now accepts `max_tool_calls=None` for this. The 31st call trips `tool_budget`, as in multi mode.

  - The answer-key runtime test now runs both modes on all 10 incidents. No assertion was weakened.
  - I set the ticket's Status to `done`, as tickets 05 and 06 did.
  
  **Open issues:**
  - The baseline re-sends its whole transcript at every step, so its token use grows roughly with the square of its tool calls. That cost is part of what the comparison measures.
  - `TerminatedBy` is still defined in both `limits.py` and `evidence_rules.py`.
  - I could not run ruff in this environment.
</agent-message>

**Current code (01–08, 12 merged):** `investigate(incident_id, llm, *, mode="multi"|"single", limits=DEFAULT_LIMITS, clock=utc_now, tool_backoff_s=...) -> Investigation{report, blackboard}` in `investigate.py`; `dataset.py` (`list_incident_ids`, `load_scenario`, `load_answer_key`, `AnswerKey` with expected_outcome `root_cause|inconclusive`, service, category, key_evidence_ids, traps); `schemas.py` (InvestigationReport: outcome `ROOT_CAUSE|INCONCLUSIVE`, ranked_hypotheses, facts, assumptions, recommended_actions, gaps, metrics{tool_calls, llm_calls, tokens_in, tokens_out, cache_tokens, latency_s}, terminated_by, rule_adjustments, failures); `llm/` (`base.py` errors: LLMError, LLMTimeoutError, LLMUnavailableError; `claude_cli.py`; `router.py` with per-role clients; `mock.py`); `cli.py`. `uv sync` in your worktree first; then `uv run pytest` (~12 s) and `uv run pyright`.

**What to build:** an `eval` console script (`uv run eval --all`, plus a way to pick incidents/systems and a run name/dir) that runs both systems (multi, single) on all 10 incidents and writes one `eval/results/<run>/<incident>__<system>.json` per pair (the report + deterministic scores; leave a clearly named place for judge scores — ticket 10 adds the judge) as soon as each pair completes, plus `eval/results/<run>/summary.md` comparing both systems: accuracy, grounding, tool calls, LLM calls, tokens in/out/cache shown separately, latency (and a placeholder column/section for judge scores). Resume: re-running skips pairs whose result file exists; write each file atomically (temp file + rename) so a pair cut off midway is never saved. On a rate-limit or usage-cap error from the LLM backend, stop cleanly after saving completed pairs, print the exact resume command, and exit non-zero; this needs a distinct, detectable error — add e.g. `LLMRateLimitError(LLMError)` in `llm/base.py` and make `claude_cli.py` raise it when the CLI's JSON/stderr indicates a rate limit/usage cap (inspect `claude_cli.py`'s error handling; match conservative markers like "rate limit", "usage limit", "429", "overloaded" and document them), and ensure the agent loop / investigate() lets it propagate instead of swallowing it as an ordinary failed attempt. Evaluation code is the one place besides `dataset.py` allowed to load answer keys: put it in its own package (e.g. `src/incident_investigator/evaluation/`) and extend the allowlist in `tests/test_answer_key_isolation.py` narrowly to that package — keep every other guard intact, and keep the "no incident IDs / answer-key service names in src" guard passing (don't hardcode incident IDs; take them from `list_incident_ids()`). Use the per-role models config by default and `--llm mock` for offline runs. Avoid adding dependencies (another agent is adding FastAPI for ticket 11 in parallel and edits `pyproject.toml`/`uv.lock`; add only the `[project.scripts]` line for `eval`).

**Do NOT run the live evaluation** against the real Claude CLI — it uses the user's subscription and the PRD assigns the full run to the user. Verify with `--llm mock` end to end (all 20 pairs, summary written, resume skips) and mocked rate-limit errors.

**Method:** test-first, red → green, one slice at a time. Agreed seams: the scorer functions on hand-built reports + answer keys (literal expected values: correct, wrong service, wrong category, inconclusive-by-design both ways, grounding with fake IDs, zero citations); the eval runner via its public function/CLI with the mock LLM and a tmp results dir (20 files written, summary present, rerun skips existing, a pair whose investigation raises midway leaves no file, a scripted rate-limit error stops cleanly with the resume command and keeps completed files). No tests of private helpers. Run pyright and single test files often; full `uv run pytest` at the end.

**Finish:** tick the ticket's truly-done checkboxes (explain any not), append a dated `## Comments` note (result file schema and where ticket 10 plugs the judge in; the exact command the user runs for the live eval and resume), and commit with message `Ticket 09: <summary>` ending with `Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Report back (under 300 words): branch, files changed, test count, the commands, the mock-run summary table, deviations, open issues.

Ticket 07 is merged. `main` now has tickets 01–08 and 12, with 270 tests passing and pyright clean. The suite runs in 11 s, down from 44 s, because tests now skip the real retry delays.

**What 07 added:**
- **Single-agent mode:** `uv run investigate <id> --mode single` runs one Opus agent with the same tools, failure schedule, limits object, evidence rules and report format as multi-agent mode. A test checks that both modes get the very same limits object, not a copy.
- **Fairness choice:** the baseline is one task, so the 6-calls-per-task cap doesn't apply to it. Its binding limit is the run's 30-call budget.
- **Token growth:** the baseline re-sends its whole conversation on every step, so its token use grows quickly with each tool call. That cost is part of what the comparison measures.

Ticket 09 (evaluation runner) and ticket 11 (HTTP API) are running now. The 09 agent will test the runner end to end with the mock only and won't start the live 20-run evaluation, because the PRD leaves that to you. Ticket 10 (LLM judge) comes after 09, then 13 (docs).

The inc07 and inc10 answer-key services still haven't been decided, so 09 is scoring against them as written: `cart-svc` and `parcelhub-api`. That's easy to change later if you disagree.

Ticket 11 is merged. `main` now has tickets 01–08, 11 and 12, with 287 tests passing and pyright clean.

**What 11 added:**
- **The API:** `uv run api` starts it on 127.0.0.1:8000, with Swagger at `/docs`.
  - `POST /investigations` starts a run, single- or multi-agent, and returns its id right away with a 202 status.
  - `GET /investigations/{id}` returns the run's status, its trace and, once finished, the report.
  - `GET /incidents` lists the 10 incidents.
- **Error handling:** an unknown incident or unknown investigation id returns 404, and a bad request body returns 422. A run that crashes ends as `failed` with an error message.
- **Storage:** every investigation is kept in memory and also saved as a JSON file. On restart, the API reloads the saved files and marks runs that were cut off as failed.
- **Inline incidents:** a report sent inline has no data behind it, so the tools find no evidence and the run ends INCONCLUSIVE.
- **Not covered:** there is no cancel endpoint. The trace only appears once a run finishes, not while it's running. The agent checked the server by hand but didn't run a real-LLM investigation through it.

I've told the ticket 09 agent (evaluation runner, still running) to pull in 11's changes before it commits. After 09 merges, I'll run ticket 10 (the LLM judge) and then ticket 13 (docs).

No tests of private helpers. Run pyright and single test files often; full `uv run pytest` at the end.

**Finish:** tick the ticket's truly-done checkboxes (explain any not), append a dated `## Comments` note (commands; judge prompt location; retry policy; known bias R5), and commit with message `Ticket 10: <summary>` ending with `Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Report back (under 300 words): branch, files changed, test count, commands, deviations, open issues.

Ticket 09 is merged. `main` now has every ticket except 10 and 13. The suite passes (337 tests) and pyright is clean.

**What 09 added:**
- **Commands:**
  - `uv run eval --all` runs both systems on all 10 incidents.
  - `uv run eval --all --llm mock` runs offline.
- **Output:** results go to `eval/results/<run>/`, one file per incident and system plus `summary.md`. Each file is saved the moment its pair finishes, and a re-run skips pairs that already have a file.

- **Scoring:**
  - **Accuracy:** the top hypothesis must match both the service and the category. inc09 counts as correct only if the outcome is INCONCLUSIVE.
  - **Grounding:** this score also counts the evidence IDs the evidence rules removed. Otherwise every report would score 100%, because the rules strip bad IDs before the report is built.
- **Mock run:** all 20 pairs wrote, and a second run skipped all 20. The mock's accuracy figures mean nothing, because the mock doesn't actually reason.

**Known gaps:**
- Only the Claude CLI backend recognises rate limits; the API-key and local-model backends don't.
- An "overloaded" (HTTP 529) response stops the run instead of retrying.
- The rate-limit check matches the CLI's current error wording, which could change.
- inc07 and inc10 are scored strictly against `cart-svc` and `parcelhub-api`, with no partial credit for naming the calling service.

Ticket 10 (the LLM judge) is running now. Ticket 13 (README, architecture diagram, technical note, transcript) is last. It needs the live evaluation results, and running the live evaluation is your step.

content.text:
Ticket 10 is merged, so `main` now has every ticket except 13. All 357 tests pass and pyright is clean.

**What 10 added:**
- **The judge:** an Opus judge scores each report on evidence support, fact/assumption separation and recommended actions (1–5 each), and says whether the system fell for the trap. It never affects accuracy.
- **Commands:**
  - `uv run eval --all` now investigates, then judges, then writes the summary.
  - `--no-judge` skips the judge.
  - `--judge-only --run <name>` judges an existing run without investigating again.
- **Retries and failures:** bad judge output gets one retry. A second failure is recorded and the run continues. A recorded failure isn't retried on a re-run unless you clear it in the result file.
- **Cost:** the judge's tokens and calls go in a separate table in `summary.md`. They never count toward either system.
- **Saving and resume:** each judgement is saved into its pair's result file. A re-run skips pairs already judged, and the judge stops cleanly on a usage cap, like the runner.

Ticket 13 (README, architecture diagram, technical note, transcript notes) is running. It won't invent evaluation numbers. The README will show where the live results go, and that checkbox stays unticked until you run the live evaluation.

The live evaluation means 20 investigations plus 20 judge calls through your subscription. The one live multi-agent run so far (inc01) took about 77 s, so expect roughly 30 to 60 minutes. If you hit a usage cap, re-run the same command and it continues where it stopped. Do you want me to start it once ticket 13 merges, or would you rather run `uv run eval --all` yourself?

All 13 tickets are built and merged into `main`. All 359 tests pass and pyright is clean. One acceptance box is still open: ticket 13's live evaluation results, because that run hasn't happened yet. Every commit is local; nothing was pushed and there is no remote.

**How the work ran:** each ticket was built by its own agent on a separate branch, test first. I merged each one and ran the full suite and typecheck after every merge. All 12 agent branches are merged and their worktrees removed. Ticket 12 and 13 are marked `ready-for-human`; the rest are marked `done`.

**What exists now:**
- **Investigation:** `uv run investigate <id> --mode multi|single` runs six agents on a shared blackboard. The two modes share the same tools, limits and evidence rules, so the comparison is fair.
- **Evaluation:** `uv run eval --all` runs both systems on all 10 incidents, scores them and has the Opus judge rate them. It saves each result as it finishes and picks up where it left off after a usage cap.
- **API:** `uv run api` serves it over HTTP, with Swagger at `/docs`.
- **Docs:** the README has setup, usage, a Mermaid architecture diagram and a list of unfinished items. A draft technical note (475 words) is in `docs/technical-note.md`.
- **Real runs so far:** only inc01, a few times during development. Multi-agent mode on Claude found the right root cause. Everything else was checked with the offline mock.

**What's left for you:**
1. **Run the live evaluation.** That's 20 investigations plus 20 judge calls on your subscription, roughly 30 to 60 minutes. Then paste the tables from `eval/results/live/summary.md` into the README placeholder. I can start it if you'd like.
2. **Review the answer keys,** especially inc07 (`cart-svc`) and inc10 (`parcelhub-api`). The root-cause service there could be argued either way, and scoring is strict.
3. **Edit and sign off the technical note.**
4. **Check `docs/transcript/` for privacy.** It contains your email, home path, company name and connected integrations. Older copies are already in git history from the first commit, so editing the files now won't remove them. If you submit the repo itself, those copies would need to be removed from history or the repo squashed. The newest transcripts are uncommitted, so commit them once you've reviewed them.
5. **Decide how to submit.**

Open issues are listed in the README's unfinished-features section. The ones that matter most:
- The offline mock gives meaningless accuracy numbers.
- Only the Claude CLI backend recognises a rate limit; the API-key and local-model backends don't.
- The 10-minute limit can't stop a model call that's already running.
- Evidence gaps never close once opened.

"""The single `investigate()` entry point shared by the CLI and (later) the API."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Literal, get_args

from pydantic import BaseModel

from incident_investigator.baseline import run_baseline
from incident_investigator.blackboard import Blackboard
from incident_investigator.dataset import load_scenario
from incident_investigator.graph import build_graph
from incident_investigator.limits import DEFAULT_LIMITS, Clock, RunGuard, RunLimits, utc_now
from incident_investigator.llm.base import LLMClient
from incident_investigator.schemas import IncidentReport, InvestigationReport, Scenario
from incident_investigator.tools import DEFAULT_BACKOFF_S, ToolSession

# Graph steps, not a run limit: a Critic loop takes about 7 steps, and LangGraph's
# default of 25 would cut a long plan with 2 loops short.
RECURSION_LIMIT = 500

Mode = Literal["multi", "single"]
"""`multi`: the multi-agent graph. `single`: the single-agent baseline (ticket 07)."""
MODES: tuple[Mode, ...] = get_args(Mode)


class Investigation(BaseModel):
    """One finished run: the report and the full blackboard (tasks, findings, trace...)."""

    report: InvestigationReport
    blackboard: Blackboard


def investigate(
    incident_id: str,
    llm: LLMClient,
    *,
    mode: Mode = "multi",
    limits: RunLimits = DEFAULT_LIMITS,
    clock: Clock = utc_now,
    tool_backoff_s: float = DEFAULT_BACKOFF_S,
) -> Investigation:
    """Run one investigation in either mode. Raises UnknownIncidentError for an unknown
    ID and ValueError for an unknown mode.

    Both modes get a ToolSession over the same scenario (same tools, same failure
    schedule), one RunGuard over the same `limits` object, the same evidence rules and
    the same report schema. The scenario goes only into the ToolSession; the blackboard
    starts with just the incident report. `limits` and `clock` (for the wall-clock limit
    and the reported latency) are injectable for tests, and so is `tool_backoff_s`, the
    base backoff between retries of a timed-out tool call (0 makes tests fast)."""
    _check_mode(mode)
    scenario = load_scenario(incident_id)
    return _run(scenario.id, scenario, llm, mode=mode, limits=limits, clock=clock, tool_backoff_s=tool_backoff_s)


INLINE_INCIDENT_ID = "inline"
"""The incident ID under which an inline incident report is investigated."""


def investigate_report(
    report: IncidentReport,
    llm: LLMClient,
    *,
    mode: Mode = "multi",
    limits: RunLimits = DEFAULT_LIMITS,
    clock: Clock = utc_now,
    tool_backoff_s: float = DEFAULT_BACKOFF_S,
) -> Investigation:
    """Investigate an incident report that is not in the dataset (the API's inline path).

    No telemetry stands behind such a report, so the tools query an empty scenario:
    every tool returns no evidence, and the evidence rules end the run INCONCLUSIVE.
    Everything else (graph or baseline, limits, rules, report) is what `investigate()`
    runs."""
    _check_mode(mode)
    # model_construct: the `incNN` ID pattern is for dataset files, not for this run.
    scenario = Scenario.model_construct(id=INLINE_INCIDENT_ID, report=report)
    return _run(INLINE_INCIDENT_ID, scenario, llm, mode=mode, limits=limits, clock=clock, tool_backoff_s=tool_backoff_s)


def _check_mode(mode: str) -> None:
    if mode not in MODES:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown mode {mode!r}; choose one of: {', '.join(MODES)}")


def _run(
    incident_id: str,
    scenario: Scenario,
    llm: LLMClient,
    *,
    mode: Mode,
    limits: RunLimits,
    clock: Clock,
    tool_backoff_s: float,
) -> Investigation:
    tools = ToolSession(scenario, backoff_s=tool_backoff_s)
    guard = RunGuard(limits, clock=clock)
    start = Blackboard(incident_id=incident_id, incident=scenario.report, started_at=guard.started_at)
    if mode == "single":
        final = run_baseline(llm, tools, start, guard=guard)
    else:
        graph = build_graph(llm, tools, guard=guard)
        final = Blackboard.model_validate(graph.invoke(start, config={"recursion_limit": RECURSION_LIMIT}))
    assert final.report is not None
    return Investigation(report=final.report, blackboard=final)

import json
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import pytest

from incident_investigator import cli, models_config
from incident_investigator.blackboard import Blackboard
from incident_investigator.cli import main
from incident_investigator.dataset import load_scenario
from incident_investigator.investigate import investigate
from incident_investigator.schemas import InvestigationReport


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def no_tool_backoff(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    """In-process CLI runs skip the real retry backoff of timed-out tool calls (speed only)."""

    def fast(*args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
        return investigate(*args, **kwargs, tool_backoff_s=0)

    monkeypatch.setattr(cli, "investigate", fast)


def test_investigate_inc01_with_mock_llm_writes_a_valid_report(tmp_path: Path):
    exit_code = main(["inc01", "--llm", "mock", "--out", str(tmp_path)])

    assert exit_code == 0
    report = InvestigationReport.model_validate_json((tmp_path / "inc01__multi.json").read_text())
    assert report.incident_id == "inc01"
    assert report.terminated_by == "done"
    # Mock plan: observability (logs, metrics, deploys) || dependency (dependencies,
    # past_incidents) -> reasoning; then the Critic asks for one observability follow-up
    # and a second reasoning pass, then is satisfied. LLM calls: 1 plan + 4 + 3 +
    # 1 reasoning + 1 critic + 4 follow-up + 1 reasoning + 1 critic + 1 reporting.
    assert report.metrics.tool_calls == 5 + 3
    assert report.metrics.llm_calls == 17
    assert len(report.ranked_hypotheses) >= 2
    assert report.recommended_actions


def test_the_full_blackboard_trace_is_saved_next_to_the_report(tmp_path: Path):
    main(["inc01", "--llm", "mock", "--out", str(tmp_path)])

    board = Blackboard.model_validate_json((tmp_path / "inc01__multi.trace.json").read_text())
    assert [(t.id, t.agent, t.status) for t in board.tasks] == [
        ("t1", "observability", "done"),
        ("t2", "dependency", "done"),
        ("t3", "reasoning", "done"),
        # The mock Critic asks for one follow-up, then is satisfied.
        ("c1.1", "observability", "done"),
        ("c1.r", "reasoning", "done"),
    ]
    assert [(t.origin, t.loop) for t in board.tasks[3:]] == [("critic", 1)] * 2
    assert board.critic_loops == 1 and len(board.critic_reviews) == 2
    spans = {t.task_id: (t.started_at, t.ended_at) for t in board.trace}
    assert spans["t1"][0] < spans["t2"][1] and spans["t2"][0] < spans["t1"][1], "t1 and t2 overlap"
    assert spans["t3"][0] >= max(spans["t1"][1], spans["t2"][1])
    assert {f.agent for f in board.findings} >= {"observability", "dependency"}
    assert board.report is not None and board.report.incident_id == "inc01"


def test_report_only_cites_evidence_that_exists_in_the_scenario(tmp_path: Path):
    main(["inc01", "--llm", "mock", "--out", str(tmp_path)])
    report = InvestigationReport.model_validate_json((tmp_path / "inc01__multi.json").read_text())

    cited = {i for f in report.facts for i in f.evidence_ids}
    cited |= {i for h in report.ranked_hypotheses for i in h.supporting_ids + h.contradicting_ids}
    assert cited, "the mock run should cite the log evidence it was given"
    assert cited <= load_scenario("inc01").evidence_ids()


def test_unknown_incident_exits_non_zero_with_a_clear_message_and_no_report(tmp_path: Path, capsys):
    exit_code = main(["inc99", "--llm", "mock", "--out", str(tmp_path)])

    assert exit_code != 0
    assert "unknown incident 'inc99'" in capsys.readouterr().err
    assert list(tmp_path.iterdir()) == []


def test_investigate_console_script_runs(tmp_path: Path):
    script = Path(sys.executable).parent / "investigate"

    done = subprocess.run(
        [str(script), "inc01", "--llm", "mock", "--out", str(tmp_path)],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        timeout=60,
    )

    assert done.returncode == 0, done.stderr
    assert (tmp_path / "inc01__multi.json").is_file()


def test_claude_cli_backend_fails_fast_when_the_cli_is_missing(tmp_path: Path, capsys, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("PATH", str(tmp_path / "empty-bin"))
    out = tmp_path / "out"

    exit_code = main(["inc01", "--llm", "claude_cli", "--out", str(out)])

    assert exit_code != 0
    assert "Claude CLI 'claude' not found" in capsys.readouterr().err
    assert not out.exists()


@pytest.fixture
def fake_claude_on_path(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch) -> Path:
    """A `claude` on PATH so the preflight finds it; subprocess.run is faked per test."""
    bin_dir = tmp_path / "bin"
    bin_dir.mkdir()
    exe = bin_dir / "claude"
    exe.write_text("#!/bin/sh\nexit 1\n")
    exe.chmod(0o755)
    monkeypatch.setenv("PATH", str(bin_dir))
    return exe


def test_claude_cli_backend_fails_fast_when_not_logged_in(tmp_path: Path, capsys, monkeypatch, fake_claude_on_path):
    def run(args: list[str], **kwargs: Any) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
        return subprocess.CompletedProcess(args, 1, json.dumps({"loggedIn": False}), "")

    monkeypatch.setattr(subprocess, "run", run)
    out = tmp_path / "out"

    exit_code = main(["inc01", "--llm", "claude_cli", "--out", str(out)])

    assert exit_code != 0
    assert "claude login" in capsys.readouterr().err
    assert not out.exists()


def test_an_agent_that_replies_garbage_twice_still_gets_a_report(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch, fake_claude_on_path):
    models_seen: list[str] = []

    def run(args: list[str], **kwargs: Any) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
        if args[1:] == ["auth", "status"]:
            return subprocess.CompletedProcess(args, 0, json.dumps({"loggedIn": True}), "")
        models_seen.append(args[args.index("--model") + 1])
        reply = {
            "type": "result",
            "is_error": False,
            "duration_ms": 900,
            "result": "Sorry, I cannot help with that.",
            "usage": {"input_tokens": 7, "output_tokens": 3, "cache_read_input_tokens": 50},
        }
        return subprocess.CompletedProcess(args, 0, json.dumps(reply), "")

    monkeypatch.setattr(subprocess, "run", run)

    exit_code = main(["inc01", "--llm", "claude_cli", "--out", str(tmp_path)])

    assert exit_code == 0
    report = InvestigationReport.model_validate_json((tmp_path / "inc01__multi.json").read_text())
    assert report.outcome == "INCONCLUSIVE"
    assert report.ranked_hypotheses == []
    # Planner x2 (then the default plan), observability x2 || dependency x2, reasoning x2.
    # No hypotheses, so the Reporting agent has nothing to recommend and is not called.
    assert report.metrics.llm_calls == 8
    assert report.metrics.tool_calls == 0
    assert report.metrics.tokens_in == 8 * 7
    assert report.metrics.tokens_out == 8 * 3
    assert report.metrics.cache_tokens == 8 * 50
    opus, haiku = "claude-opus-5-5", "claude-haiku-5-5"
    assert models_seen[:2] == [opus, opus]
    assert models_seen[2:6] == [haiku] * 4
    assert models_seen[6:] == [opus, opus]


# --- Backend choice: the models config by default, --llm as a global override (ticket 12) ---


def _models_toml(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch, body: str) -> None:
    """Point every load_models() call (CLI and graph) at a temporary models.toml."""
    path = tmp_path / "models.toml"
    path.write_text(body)
    monkeypatch.setattr(models_config, "DEFAULT_PATH", path)


ALL_ROLES = ["planner", "reasoning", "critic", "baseline", "judge", "observability", "dependency", "reporting"]


def test_without_llm_the_backend_comes_from_the_models_config(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch):
    roles = "\n".join(f'{r} = {{ backend = "mock", model = "claude-haiku-5-5" }}' for r in ALL_ROLES)
    _models_toml(tmp_path, monkeypatch, f"[roles]\n{roles}\n")
    out = tmp_path / "out"

    exit_code = main(["inc01", "--out", str(out)])

    assert exit_code == 0
    report = InvestigationReport.model_validate_json((out / "inc01__multi.json").read_text())
    assert report.metrics.llm_calls == 17


def test_the_default_config_uses_claude_cli_and_fails_fast_without_it(tmp_path: Path, capsys, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("PATH", str(tmp_path / "empty-bin"))
    out = tmp_path / "out"

    exit_code = main(["inc01", "--out", str(out)])

    assert exit_code == 3
    assert "Claude CLI 'claude' not found" in capsys.readouterr().err
    assert not out.exists()


def test_an_unknown_backend_in_the_models_config_fails_at_startup(tmp_path: Path, capsys, monkeypatch):
    roles = "\n".join(f'{r} = {{ backend = "gpt-cloud", model = "x" }}' for r in ALL_ROLES)
    _models_toml(tmp_path, monkeypatch, f"[roles]\n{roles}\n")
    out = tmp_path / "out"

    exit_code = main(["inc01", "--out", str(out)])

    assert exit_code == 3
    assert "unknown backend 'gpt-cloud'" in capsys.readouterr().err
    assert not out.exists()


def test_anthropic_api_without_a_key_fails_fast(tmp_path: Path, capsys, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.delenv("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", raising=False)
    out = tmp_path / "out"

    exit_code = main(["inc01", "--llm", "anthropic_api", "--out", str(out)])

    assert exit_code == 3
    assert "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is not set" in capsys.readouterr().err
    assert not out.exists()


def test_openai_compat_with_no_server_fails_fast(tmp_path: Path, capsys, monkeypatch):
    # Port 9 (discard) on loopback: nothing listens, so the connection is refused at once.
    monkeypatch.setenv("OPENAI_COMPAT_BASE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:9/v1")
    out = tmp_path / "out"

    exit_code = main(["inc01", "--llm", "openai_compat", "--out", str(out)])

    assert exit_code == 3
    err = capsys.readouterr().err
    assert "no OpenAI-compatible endpoint reachable at http://127.0.0.1:9/v1" in err
    assert not out.exists()

skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/<user>/.claude/skills/mp-code-review

Two-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:

- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?
- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?

Both axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings. Start every sub-agent with a fresh context window.

The issue tracker should have been provided to you. If not, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.

## Process

### 1. Pin the fixed point

Whatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.

Capture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.

Before going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.

### 2. Identify the spec source

Look for the originating spec, in this order:

1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in the tracker doc.
2. A path the user passed as an argument.
3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.
4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report "no spec available".

### 3. Identify the standards sources

Search the repo for every file that documents how code should be written. When `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md` exists, it must be on the list.

On top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:

- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.
- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic ("possible Feature Envy"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.

Each smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:

- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.
- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.
- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.
- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.
- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.
- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.
- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.
- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.
- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.
- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.
- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.
- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.

### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel

Issue both sub-agent calls together, in the foreground, and aggregate the reports they return.

**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:

- The full diff command and commit list.
- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).
- The brief: "Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words."

**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:

- The diff command and commit list.
- The path or fetched contents of the spec.
- The brief: "Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words."

If the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.

### 5. Aggregate

Present the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).

End with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.

## Why two axes

A change can pass one axis and fail the other:

- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**
- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**

Reporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.

# Test-Driven Development

TDD is the red → green loop. This skill is the reference that makes that loop produce tests worth keeping: what a good test is, where tests go, the anti-patterns, and the rules of the loop. Every section applies on every cycle: consult them before and during the loop, not after.

When exploring the codebase, read `GLOSSARY.md` (if it exists) so test names and interface vocabulary match the project's domain language, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.

## What a good test is

Tests verify behavior through public interfaces, not implementation details. Code can change entirely; tests shouldn't. A good test reads like a specification: "user can checkout with valid cart" tells you exactly what capability exists, and it survives refactors because it doesn't care about internal structure.

See [tests.md](tests.md) for examples and [mocking.md](mocking.md) for mocking guidelines.

## Seams: where tests go

A **seam** is the public boundary you test at: the interface where you observe behavior without reaching inside. Tests live at seams, never against internals.
